speakers: Rasvan, captioned 'Raswan Reming' (director of investment solutions, Aspect Capital)
summary: Top Traders Unplugged 149 (April 2025): Aspect's investment solutions director discusses portable alpha with CTAs as the alpha source on equity beta (Aspect paper 'Finding the Right Match'), behavioral fit, total portfolio approach, the 2025 macro divergence for trend following, CTA replication, and tailored solutions. Main conclusion: CTAs paired with equity beta give cash-efficient, adaptive, tail-resilient exposure that sits better than equity market neutral on shared tail risk.

coverage.note: nothing actionable: career background and introduction of portable alpha topic
portable alpha definition, GFC failures, 2022 private markets liquidity squeeze
career risk, CTA as shock absorber, cash efficiency, sizing of PA structure
static equity beta, cyclical vs structural reasons, return stacking, tail behavior
CTA bucket problem, equity sleeve overlay, hedging strategies bleed
trend as long-term yet crisis relief, behavioral hold, ripples after equity corrections
hidden skew in packaging, trend allows owning equities, equity market neutral comparison
antifragile caveat, shared tail risk, macro shift to volatility
policy divergence, currency trends, fixed income decoupling, stagflation whiffs
outlook of divergence; total portfolio approach definition
TPA implementation hurdles, portable alpha as bridge, CTA bucket fit, replication intro
tailored solutions vs finished products, manager relationships
investor utility, limits of customization, building blocks
managed accounts, combos of strategies; outro

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: The principle being that when you do that you get a more efficient portfolio. It works harder for you.
claims.claim: Portable alpha packages chosen beta exposures with an overlay of uncorrelated alpha, making the portfolio more efficient per dollar of capital.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: a lot of the original portable alpha implementations shared a a common left tail
claims.claim: Original portable alpha products (GFC era) used extreme leverage and shared a common left tail, so simulation of uncorrelated streams looked good but live structures broke in a crisis.
claims.conditions: extreme leverage and shared left tail

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: not enough cash buffers left to to finance the the the um ongoing structure. It meant that they had to be unwound at the worst time possible.
claims.claim: Insufficient cash buffers forced portable alpha structures to unwind at the worst time, so cash-efficiency and margin buffers determine survival.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: they want to make their liquid part of their portfolio work harder
claims.claim: After 2022, allocators heavy in private markets want their liquid portfolio to work harder.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: you now have to source those meet those liabilities from a diminished liquid as uh sort of portion of your portfolio
claims.claim: In 2022 stocks and bonds fell while private market cash flows dried up, forcing endowments and liability-driven investors to meet liabilities from a diminished liquid portfolio.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: you couple that experience of needing to make your liquid portion work harder with the career risk of selling down your equity
claims.claim: Allocators need diversification but face career risk from underweighting a strongly performing equity market, so they want to diversify equities while staying fully invested.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: portable alpha is just a mechanism, another mechanism of allowing people to access these strategies without having to make big wholesale changes to their strategic allocations
claims.claim: Portable alpha lets investors add CTAs without changing strategic asset allocation.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: by being margin traded, there's a lot of unencumbered cash floating around in your portfolio
claims.claim: CTAs are margin-traded and so leave most capital unencumbered, enabling cash-efficient overlays.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: the worse market gets, the more volatile, the more stressed the markets get, the general tendency for CTAs is to to take cover or to or to or to become more and more cashri.
claims.claim: In stress, CTAs reduce risk and move to cash (volatility targeting), a self-healing property that helps overlay structures survive shocks.
claims.conditions: sharp gap moves can still hurt

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: with 15 to $25 in a 100, you can get access to a decent uh well diversified CTA strategy. with another $ 15 to $20, you could replicate $100 notion of equity exposure
claims.claim: Per 100 of capital, about 15-25 can fund a diversified CTA and 15-20 can fund 100 notional of equity exposure, leaving ample cash for variation margin.
claims.conditions: conservative structure needed for 1-2 day drops

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: suddenly you've got a home for a CTA without having to disrupt the portfolio
claims.claim: Mid-size allocators with static equity beta can host a CTA via portable alpha without portfolio disruption.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the S&P's done, you know, 14 and a half% for the last 5 years and probably done that for the last 15 years
claims.claim: A strong S&P makes standalone CTAs look unattractive, so blending with equity beta (return stacking) makes them more acceptable.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: The idea of using derivatives to have a portfolio that's more than 100% in in in the kind of simplest terms is been to my mind more widely understood and been embraced by a broader set of investors
claims.claim: Return stacking is now more widely understood and embraced by a broader investor base such as RIAs.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: it's the tail behavior that decides how viable the structure will be
claims.claim: Viability of a portable alpha structure depends on the tail behavior of the alpha and beta together, not any alpha with any beta.
claims.indicator: tail dependence of alpha and beta

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: there's a group of investors that traditionally just wouldn't have had allocations to CTAs
claims.claim: Portable alpha brings in new investors who had no slot for CTAs.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: The things that we add as a as a strategy is how adaptive we are. How you know that we are not fitted to being defensive or growth.
claims.claim: A CTA is both defensive and growth; its value is adaptability, though a pure growth or pure defensive asset would do better in those single roles.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: there's a lot of interest from the equity sleeves. Think of it, you can decide how much overlay you put on top and then it becomes a tracking error question and a risk appetite question
claims.claim: Equity beta is the best base for a CTA overlay, and equity sleeves or a CIO completion portfolio set the overlay size as a tracking error choice.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: By default, hedging strategies are only successful if you have a short-term mindset because uh it you it's simply the returns bleed or or you lose money over time
claims.claim: Pure hedging or tail-risk strategies bleed returns over time unless timed perfectly, so they suit only short-term mindsets.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: It has the ability to deliver uh some relief uh in terms of positive performance uh during time frames um where it's most needed
claims.claim: Trend following needs a long-term holding mindset yet adapts quickly enough to deliver relief in many crises, making it a good match for long-term equity investors.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: the trend being like a medicine that requires time to work
claims.claim: The main difficulty of holding a CTA is behavioral: it is uncorrelated and zigzags at different times to the widely held equity market.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: Twothirds of the time it's an up month. Uh in a CTA you closer to 50/50.
claims.claim: Equities have positive months about two-thirds of the time while a CTA is closer to 50/50, and with loss aversion (3x) separate line items make the CTA harder to hold.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: It starts to, you know, cause ripples in currencies, in bonds, as central banks react, commodity markets react. It's those ripples that trend followers capture.
claims.claim: A big equity correction propagates to currencies, bonds and commodities; trend followers earn from those ripples rather than from equity shorts alone.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: positive skeess that you get with trend with more frequent but smaller negative months, they can get hidden in inverted commas behind this widely held asset class
claims.claim: Combined with equity beta, trend's frequent small losses are hidden behind the widely held equity asset class while positive skew remains, making it behaviorally easier to hold.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: it's the packaging that really talks to behavioral need rather than a a a logical construct
claims.claim: The alpha source should remain independent of equities; packaging with beta is a behavioral accommodation, not a logical construct.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: trend following is what allows you to own equities
claims.claim: Trend following lets investors own equities.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's going to be harder and harder to be that diversifier if you do that because we know equities is the part of the portfolio that's going to um struggle the most
claims.claim: Making trend portfolios 50% single-stock equities weakens diversification since equities struggle most when diversification is needed; prefer classically diversified portfolios.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: I think it's overwhelmingly equity market neutral strategies that are being utilized.
claims.claim: Equity market neutral is overwhelmingly the alpha used in portable alpha; managed futures is the novel alternative Aspect proposes.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: if it's a sharp drop and I'm long that market and it gaps against me, guess what? I'm not going to be providing protection.
claims.claim: CTAs are only almost antifragile: a sharp gap against a long position gives no protection, so a cash buffer is needed.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: what they can't really sidestep is the shared tail risk that hits equity markets
claims.claim: Equity market neutral keeps shared equity tail risk, while a CTA overlay gives greater tracking error but a mechanical cross-asset response when equities shock.
claims.direction: CTA over EMN for equity tail

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: it's all the other asset classes that drove performance with a little bit of a contribution eventually from stock indices
claims.claim: In the GFC, pandemic crash and tech wreck, CTA gains came mainly from other asset classes reacting, with only a small contribution from stock indices.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: now we've gone into this decade and we've had, you know, much more volatility in GDP, much more volatility in inflation, uh, higher interest rates
claims.claim: The 2010s of secular stagnation and low macro volatility gave way to higher macro volatility, favoring CTAs.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: indices that actually quantitatively track uncertainty are at multi-year highs and, um, all of that would seem to be a favorable backdrop for for CTAs
claims.claim: Uncertainty indices at multi-year highs suggest more dislocations, a favorable backdrop for CTAs (uncertainty alpha), though returns were muted since 2022.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: the sheer amount of potential policy changes and also potential policy mishaps on the US has actually really put a question mark on this US
claims.claim: In early 2025 German fiscal expansion, US policy shifts and DeepSeek changed the outlook for Europe, US tech and Asia, creating sources of big macro trends.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: we're not fitted. I have no prior. I have no sense of the fair value
claims.claim: CTAs have no prior, fair-value view or geographic bias, so can follow whichever divergence emerges.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: currency markets currencies were pretty uninteresting asset class from a trend following point of view during this this this QE era
claims.claim: During the zero-rate QE era currencies gave little trend following return because coordinated policy suppressed risk appetite.
claims.indicator: FX trend returns in QE era

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: the currency asset class was the one that picked up that divergence and drove returns and dispersion for the next two to three years
claims.claim: When inflation built and monetary policies diverged across regions in 2021-22, currencies became the main driver of CTA returns for two to three years.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: I think right now we've seen a very big decoupling of fixed income markets between US treasuries buns bank of Japan is sort of still a little bit different
claims.claim: In 2025 fixed income markets decoupled (Treasuries, Bunds, JGBs) and China shifted to risk-on, creating breeding grounds for sustained macro divergence.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: once there is a little bit of clarity of this divergence, we should see opportunities open up
claims.claim: Uncertainty leads to short-term inactivity and choppiness, but clear divergence later creates trend opportunities.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: I definitely got some whiffs of stagflation from the Fed's sort of results last night
claims.claim: The March 2025 FOMC revised growth down with inflation still elevated, hinting at stagflation.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: And so what I would like to see happen over the next six month 12 months is divergence.
claims.claim: Aspect expects divergence over the next 6-12 months, being optimistic medium-term while cautious on liquidity, risk management and sensible model choices in the short term.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you're optimizing within a category without being cognizant of what everybody else in the portfolio is doing
claims.claim: Strategic allocation silos optimize within asset classes while ignoring portfolio-wide interactions.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: taking the portfolio and looking through to the underlying risk factors uh and then optimizing and deciding how to allocate risk based on that
claims.claim: The total portfolio approach looks through to risk factors and allocates risk rather than buckets, used by larger endowments, SWFs and pensions.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: Organizations that have adopted this approach tend to find greater utility and a greater applicability of of CTAs
claims.claim: Organizations using the total portfolio approach find CTAs more useful because CTAs are best judged at portfolio level.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: but are still siloed in the asset classes are trying to make those individual asset classes become sort of work harder
claims.claim: Organizations unable to adopt TPA use portable alpha within existing sleeves to move toward the same result without restructuring.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: the hedge fund team says to you, you've got too much variable beta.
claims.claim: A CTA does not fit a single asset-class bucket (hedge fund team wants low beta, equity team wants equities), hence the bucket problem.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: it's at least one and a half to 2% perom you could outperform by having a a total portfolio approach versus an SAA approach
claims.claim: Consultants estimate TPA outperforms strategic asset allocation by 1.5-2% per year.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: doesn't it doesn't replicate that closely um and correlation to the indices tend to break down at critical times
claims.claim: CTA replication products do not replicate closely, and their correlation to CTA indices breaks down at critical times.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: they're quite narrow very few markets you're taking a manager risk
claims.claim: Replication products trade few markets and take manager risk, so they may not capture trend following properties.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: as long as we don't have a spectacular unwind or or or big riskmanagement mishap from one of these replicated strategies that will taint the space
claims.claim: A blow-up in a replicated strategy could harm the whole CTA industry's reputation.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: model portfolios have the ability to create investable ETFbased portfolios that have a slice allocate to manage futures
claims.claim: ETF-based model portfolios with managed futures slices broaden CTA awareness and adoption.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: shouldn't there be some quote unquote, you know, rules about what a product should contain in order to be called a CTA product
claims.claim: Industry labels all futures-trading products as CTA, so definitional standards may be needed.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: there is a merit in really understanding the manager's approach so that when they have their their draw down you understand that
claims.claim: Allocators benefit from deep relationships with a few managers: they understand drawdowns better and can net fees across products.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you might want to say well we want to have bestin-class in every bucket and that's where it might make sense to do it individually
claims.claim: Best-in-class selection per bucket argues for individual manager selection instead of one provider.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it seems that investors value that given the growth of the multistrats which are all based on delivering consistent returns
claims.claim: Investors value consistency and avoiding sharp drawdowns over maximum compound growth, as seen in multistrat growth.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: Maybe they want to just do the commodities part of it. That's what's missing. Or maybe they just want to do the non-trend part of it.
claims.claim: Allocators with an existing portfolio want sleeves of a CTA program (commodities only, non-trend only) to complete the portfolio.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: You want to preserve the integrity of the investment thesis.
claims.claim: Customization should keep the strategy pure: do not speed up the portfolio or overweight carry on request.

claims.speaker: Rasvan (captioned Raswan Reming)
claims.quote: a greater um sort of growth area has been in allocators combining a number of our strategies
claims.claim: Allocators increasingly combine several strategies in their own proportions rather than tuning each strategy.
